A bigger update: control over your queue, notes on songs, lyrics with romanization, and a library without voice notes.

## New

- **Play next and Add to queue.** Long press a song, album, artist or playlist, or tap its three dots. In the player's queue, drag the handle to reorder and swipe left to remove a song.
- **Notes on songs.** Write a short note on a song, like where it takes you back to. It shows under the title in the player, and a small icon marks the song in Songs.
- **Romanization and translations in lyrics.** When a `.lrc` file has a second line with the same time, it shows smaller under the lyric. Word-by-word highlighting still works on the main line.
- **Usually at this hour.** Home learns which songs you play at which time of day and suggests them around that hour. It appears after you have listened for a while.
- **Songs you keep skipping stay out of the suggestions** on Home.
- **Every artist gets credit.** A song by "A feat. B" now shows up on the pages of both A and B, instead of creating a new artist for the pair.
- **Haptic feedback.** A light tap when you favourite, open a menu or jump by letter. You can turn it off in Settings > General.

## Your library

- **Voice notes, recordings and ringtones are hidden.** Clips under 30 seconds that don't belong to an album, and folders like WhatsApp Voice Notes or Recordings, no longer mix with your music. Nothing is deleted. Change this, or hide more folders, in Settings > Storage > Hide from library.

## Improved

- **Swiping the player down** now shows the page you came from behind it, slowly coming back into focus.
- **The player's background** is lighter on the phone, so it stays smooth while lyrics scroll.
- **The app icon** shows correctly in the media notification, the lock screen and the audio output picker, instead of a white square.
- **"Could not reach GitHub"** now suggests switching networks. Some home Wi-Fi routers sometimes fail to find GitHub; mobile data usually works.

Your notes, listening hours and skips are stored only on your device, like the rest of your library.
